convergenceSignals.note: Full independent re-derivation of the classification table (per this iteration's own mandate, not a spot-check of the builder's table) was performed against every pure function in the Purity Boundary Map: isSelfFunded/selfFundedReasons, computeColonySurplusUsd, computePerCitizenSurplusUsd, filterProductiveCitizens, deriveRecentSpawnAttempts, countChildrenProvisioning, deriveMeasuredShelterCostUsd, decideColonySpawn, buildChildSpec/nextChildId, isLockStale (pre-existing, out of scope), selectCloudTarget, needsSolanaWallet, readCitizenBalances, resolveEvmPrivateKey/resolveSolanaSecret, ensureAgentId, and computeSpawnGate (pre-existing) -- roughly 34 (function, parameter) pairs in total, matching the builder's own table's scope exactly. The two tables agree on 33 of 34 rows. The ONE discrepancy -- decideColonySpawn's colonySurplusUsd, which the builder classified DERIVED-BOUND but which independent re-verification shows lacks the explicit 'never hand-assembled, always the direct return value of X()' binding sentence AND lacks a dedicated real-derivation proof obligation that every other DERIVED-BOUND parameter in this exact function (recentSpawnAttempts, childrenProvisioning) and every sibling instance of this recurring failure class (deployTarget, filterProductiveCitizens's own ledgerRows/citizens) received -- is a genuine, well-evidenced gap, not a manufactured one: it is the SAME recurring failure class, in the SAME function, sitting directly beside two parameters that DID get the fix, and the builder's own table applies the correct rigorous standard to a structurally identical case one row earlier (row 133-134) before inconsistently relaxing it for colonySurplusUsd one row later (row 140). This answers this iteration's central question directly: the failure class has NOT genuinely converged, and the structured checklist methodology itself still has a blind spot -- specifically, it is vulnerable to accepting weaker evidence (a bare conceptual/EARS-clause tie-in) for one row of a table while correctly demanding the full binding-sentence-plus-PROP standard for a structurally identical row elsewhere in the SAME document, even within the SAME reviewer's own single pass. This is the SIXTH instance of this exact failure class found across iterations 14-18 (recentSpawnAttempts -> childrenProvisioning -> measured_last_shelter_cost_usd -> deployTarget+initialSkills -> filterProductiveCitizens's own ledgerRows/citizens -> decideColonySpawn's own colonySurplusUsd), not the fifth, and it was found on the SAME function (decideColonySpawn) whose OTHER two comparable parameters were already fixed in the FIND-1101/1401/1501 line of work -- meaning a future sweep should specifically re-examine, with equal skepticism, every parameter of every function that has ALREADY had at least one sibling parameter fixed for this exact reason, since this is precisely where this iteration's gap was found. Separately, as a normal fresh skeptical pass over the rest of the spec (REQ-101 through REQ-403) found no other class of defect: the wallet-verification chain (PROP-105g/h/i, FIND-601/702/801), the lock's staggered-race scope (PROP-103e, FIND-1201), the dual-chain balance handling (PROP-101f/g/h, FIND-404/503/604), the co-funding ceiling logic (PROP-304f/101i, FIND-1102/1202), the Akash/Nosana secrets-injection and funding-route corrections (FIND-401-403/502), and the REQ-403 explicit-env/COORDINATOR_HOME discipline (FIND-603/701/802) all remain internally consistent and adequately proof-obligated on this fresh read -- the ONE finding above is isolated and specific, not symptomatic of broader rot in an otherwise mature, 17-iterations-hardened document.
